thread.title: Amazon (AMZN) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Amazon (AMZN) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
If it appears that everybody loves Amazon ( AMZN ), that’s because they do — at least, that’s what its share price has been telling investors all year.
Amazon stock, which on Wednesday hit a new all-time high of $1,863.84, has marched higher for most of 2018 (up almost 55% YTD), save for a few dips here and there. And the company, which is set to report second quarter earnings after the closing Thursday, is now the verge of achieving a $1 trillion market cap, trailing Apple ( AAPL ) by only a slim margin. Will its earnings results be enough of a catalyst to push Amazon beyond that historic threshold?
In the three months that ended June, the Seattle-based company is expected to earn earn $2.50 per share on revenue of $53.38 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 40 cents per share on revenue of $37.95 billion. For the full year, ending in December, EPS is expected to rise 175% year over year to $12.56 per share, while full year revenue of $237.34 billion would rise 33.4% year over year.
The company has crushed its earnings estimates in the past three quarters. And management last quarter issued Q2 guidance for revenue to come in the range of $51 billion to $54 billion, while operating income would be between $1.1 billion to $1.9 billion. Both measures, at the midpoint, would only be inline with expectations. Given the strong performance of AMZN stock, that won’t be enough to keep the Street happy.
But here’s the thing: The retail giant recently announced that Prime Day 2018 was its largest shopping event in its history, outpacing not only Prime Day 2017, but also Cyber Monday and Black Friday. There’s a good chance that much of these sales will boost this quarter’s earnings as well as the third quarter. Beyond the top- and bottom-line results, all eyes will be on the performance of its Cloud platform AWS (Amazon Web Services), which has been and continues to be the company’s cash cow.
In the first quarter, Amazon reported a 48.6% revenue growth in AWS, reaching $5.44 billion, while operating income grew 57% to $1.4 billion. While Microsoft is indeed encroaching on Amazon’s market share, Wall Street continues to expect the AWS business to grow at around 40% year over year. Assuming AWS grows in a range of 45% to 47% this quarter, that translates to total revenue around $6 billion, enough to surpass Street forecast of $5.98 billion.
Citing strong cloud computing momentum, Piper Jaffray recently raised its 12-month price target from $1,850 to $2,075, while Credit Suisse upped its target from $1,950 to $2,000. Meanwhile, Brent Thill, analysts at Jefferies, sees AWS surging despite increased competition, saying the platform can still rise 200% and crossing $60 billion in annual revenue by 2023. And it would seem Amazon’s bright future is the reason the stock is so loved.
